text:
Lia (support): FYI, customer (Acme) rotated their API keys via Vault an hour ago and we're still seeing 403s from some of their traffic. They say metadata service shows new key active. 

Lia (support): repro steps they gave:
- rotated key in Vault (kv-v2)
- updated app secret reference (using Hashi sidecar)
- kicked a rolling restart (helm rollout restart)
- still ~10% requests get 403 errors

Lia (support): attached curl logs from their edge node:
```
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_newkey...' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden\n{ "error": "invalid_api_key" }
```

Rajesh (eng): thanks — first guess: partial propagation / some hosts still caching old key mapping. Do they use our edge auth cache or are they calling directly to main API?

Lia (support): they go through our edge layer (edge-proxy). We deploy edge-proxy as fleet of instances behind LB. They reported spikes correlate with a subset of nodes (we have their IP ranges).

Maya (sre): can we check edge auth cache TTL + whether revocation was broadcast? When a key is revoked we push a signed revocation event to the cache invalidation topic. If some edge nodes missed it (partition), they'd accept old key until local TTL expires.

Rajesh (eng): good point. I can query the revocation topic and the last broadcast offset. Also need to confirm Vault actually rotated both primary and the read-only alias used by long-lived workers. Sometimes teams keep old alias in env var.

Alex (infra): quick checklist I'm running now:
- check vault audit for rotate + revoke events for that key id
- query ks-messaging topic offsets for "key-revocations"
- list edge-proxy pods on the nodes the customer reported
- check sidecar logs for stash-refresh failures

DeployBot: [deploy status] rollout/edge-proxy  -> 43/43 pods ready. (timestamp 1767440400)

Rajesh (eng): I pulled vault audit: rotation event at 1767439500, and revoke for old key at 1767439550. Looks normal. Messaging topic shows a gap on a single partition between offsets 78291-78293 (one consumer lagged) at 1767439605.

Maya (sre): that matches. Which consumers were lagged? If the invalidation consumer on cluster-us-east-1 was down, those edge nodes wouldn't drop the old key until TTL.

Alex (infra): consumer group "edge-revoker" had one pod crashed (OOMKilled) and restarted by k8s at 1767439900. The restarted consumer resumed but there was ~2m gap. Some edge-proxies kept accepting old key until their local cache TTL (5m) expired. Could cause intermittent 403s depending on request routing.

Lia (support): customer says errors persisted ~20 minutes after rotation, not 2-3. Any other factor?

Rajesh (eng): possibility: some of their requests hit an older layer: we have an nginx ingress that caches upstream headers for 15 minutes for performance (we set proxy_cache_key on auth header for a microcache). If an ingress edge route had a stale auth->session mapping, it might forward old auth metadata. Also check CDN edge TTL and any API keys cached in WAF rules.

Maya (sre): rollup: two issues seen in the wild with rotations causing this type of symptom:
- propagation gap: invalidation message missed -> local caches accept old key until TTL.
- external caches (CDN, WAF) holding mapping longer than expected.

Alex (infra): I grepped ingress logs for the customer IPs. Found several requests going through an old ingress pod running an older config (we had a delayed config rollout to that node). That pod still had proxy_cache inactive flag false, and one of its routes had disk cache TTL 900s.

Rajesh (eng): ok. Immediate mitigation ideas:
- force a purge of key caches for affected edge nodes (invalidate local store)
- restart the edge-proxy pods serving the reported IP ranges (fast but heavier)
- purge CDN / WAF cache for the customer's key mapping (if applicable)

Maya (sre): I pushed an invalidation re-broadcast for the revoked key id to the topic and manually triggered consumer group rebalance. Also kicked `kubectl rollout restart deployment/edge-proxy -n prod --field-selector spec.nodeName=...` for the few affected nodes.

Lia (support): customer acknowledged a drop in 403s after your invalidation push (~5 minutes later). They still saw a couple of errors (3/500 requests) then resolved.

Rajesh (eng): long term: we should add these actions to our rotation runbook:
- 1) rotate key in Vault (kv-v2)
- 2) ensure revocation event written + acked by messaging (monitor offsets for all partitions)
- 3) verify consumer group lags = 0 before marking rotation complete
- 4) trigger config rollout or cache purge for ingress/CDN/WAF where auth mapping cached
- 5) helper script to query all edge nodes for currently accepted key fingerprint

Maya (sre): agree. Also add alerting: when a revoke event is published, if any consumer lag > 0 for more than 30s, page infra oncall. We had a transient OOM that took kube to restart, which is fine, but we need faster detection.

Alex (infra): I'll create a small job that polls `edge-revoker` consumer lags and posts to our ops channel if lag > 0. Also tightening local cache default TTL to 60s for auth keys is worth discussing — tradeoff with performance but reduces rotation window.

Lia (support): for the customer's case we offered a credit and explained root cause. They accepted. I've documented repro and steps in the ticket.

Rajesh (eng): follow-ups assigned:
- Alex: infra task for consumer lags job + reduce TTL proposal (ETA: 2d)
- Maya: add runbook step + alert (ETA: 1d)
- Rajesh: small script to scan edge nodes for accepted key fingerprints + add to rotation tool (ETA: 3d)

Lia (support): closing the thread once the infra PRs are in. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:

DeployBot: [action] created issue #INF-4829 "edge auth consumer lag detection" by Alex (1767441200)

Maya (sre): note for postmortem: this wasn't a code bug, but an operational gap (consumer resiliency + cache TTL mismatch). Will add short blameless note to incidents repo.

Rajesh (eng): fine. Also a quick note to docs: when rotating keys, remind customers about any client-side caches they control (SDKs, mobile apps, proxies) that might hold keys or session tokens beyond server TTLs.

Lia (support): got it. I'll update the support KB with the mitigation steps and link INF-4829.

Alex (infra): PR opened for lag detector -> https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/274 (stack: consumer-exporter -> prometheus alert).

Lia (support): thanks all. marking resolved in Slack. :white_check_mark:"
